properties.name: QualityGate is removed from the schema — the first type this project has ever retired, and the first stamp move that is not additive
properties.rationale:
Retiring a type is cheap to do and expensive to do badly, and the expensive part is not the deletion — it is everything that quietly referenced it. The references split three ways and each wanted a different answer: live code and live docs updated, dated analyses left untouched, and one comment rewritten because it cited the retired type as a PRECEDENT for a still-true fact (the schema has no list type) rather than as a live reference.

The two drifting lists found along the way are the more durable finding. Both were hand-maintained sets with no check that their entries were still earned, and both had already gone stale — the third and fourth instances of that class in one day, after `constructors_preserve.rs` drawing its membership on call names and the vocabulary-reach baseline needing the same discipline. The pattern is now specific enough to state: WHERE THIS PROJECT KEEPS A LIST OF EXCEPTIONS OR MEMBERS BY HAND, IT NEEDS AN ASSERTION THAT EACH ENTRY IS STILL TRUE, NOT ONLY THAT THE SET IS COVERED.

WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: whether any consumer graph anywhere holds a QualityGate instance. It cannot be checked from this repo, which is why the upgrade action states the consequence and the remedy rather than claiming the removal is safe.
properties.summary:
The type, its entry in the preserve list, its exemption in the constructor sweep, and its rows in the live coverage matrix and the loop model are gone. Node types 29 → 28. `dec:qualitygate-is-retired-the-phase-gate-dissolved-into-the-detectors` carries the ruling, what the type was FOR, and the condition under which it should return.

WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY LEFT ALONE. `docs/built-right-review.md` and `docs/reflow-v3-nuggets.md` still name it. Both are DATED ANALYSES, correct precisely because they do not track the design — the same distinction `self_host_uses_documents.py` draws between a file that must stay in step and a dated observation. Editing them would falsify a record of what was true when it was written. The CHANGELOG's historical entries are untouched for the same reason.

⚠️ THE MIGRATION CONSEQUENCE IS REAL AND WAS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. Every prior stamp move in this project was ADDITIVE, and additive moves leave an older graph readable. This one does not. A probe document carrying an undeclared node type was refused with "Unknown node type" and nothing was written, because import validates types and is all-or-nothing. So an export holding a QualityGate stops importing. The CHANGELOG carries a REQUIRED upgrade action saying so, and the reason is recorded at the assertion in schema.rs where the next person to move that number will meet it.

TWO OTHER HAND-MAINTAINED LISTS WERE FOUND DRIFTING WHILE DOING THIS, AND BOTH ARE THE SAME CLASS AS THE constructors_preserve.rs SCOPE ERROR FIXED HOURS EARLIER.

(1) THE CONSTRUCTOR SWEEP'S EXEMPTION LIST. `NO_CONSTRUCTOR` is consumed by a `continue`, so an entry that has stopped being true is skipped in silence and the list can only ever drift toward exempting more than it should. THREE OF ITS FOUR ENTRIES WERE ALREADY DEAD: `Actor` read "there is no add_actor to give a parameter to" while `add_actor` had shipped hours earlier taking a description; `EnvironmentRule` named a type that declares no description at all and so could never have been swept; `QualityGate` was about to leave the schema. A reverse sweep now fails on any exemption no longer earned, and was proven by negative control — reinstating the stale `Actor` entry fails the test naming it exactly.

(2) THE DOC CLAIMS ABOUT THE SCHEMA'S SIZE. Moving the node count exposed that the EDGE count in the same four sentences had been wrong for weeks — three said 60 and one said 64 against a real 65 — because nothing checked them. check_doc_versions.py guarded three version claims and no structural ones. It now reads both counts from schema/*.yaml and asserts them across AGENTS.md, README.md, docs/overview.md and docs/interaction-surfaces.md, matching EVERY occurrence per file so one sentence cannot rot while another stays true. Guarded claims 3 → 11.

⭐ THE SWEEP FOR OTHER HARDCODED COUNTS IS WHY THIS DID NOT COST A CI FAILURE. Two Rust assertions failed locally and naming only those would have been the one-step-over habit this project has recorded as costing four CI failures. Grepping for the number instead found three more: two source doc-comments and `tools/smoke_mcp.py`, which is a CI gate and would have failed on the push.
